name: Claude generation latency (fixed packet)
queries: Why are founder CEOs becoming harder for boards to remove?
notes: Isolates Claude generation by replaying one saved Exa packet on every trial of every arm - no Exa call, no search latency, identical evidence everywhere. Same query, packet shape, system prompt, 25-word sentence-boundary chunk rule, model and 220-token ceiling as the verified replication. Arm 1 is that replication byte for byte. Arms 2 and 3 each change exactly ONE thing from it - thinking disabled, or effort low - so whichever wins, it is known which lever won. Arm 4 combines both plus a first-sentence directive that asks for a fuller opening sentence, never a shorter one. Every first chunk is saved so the arms can be read side by side: a latency win that costs quality is not a win.
